look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · Find the BRIGHT YELLOW five-lobed flower and examine the anthers: FOUR shorter yellow anthers plus ONE much LONGER CURVED, often dark-tipped anther. Then confirm the DEEPLY CUT leaves and sharp straw-colored prickles on stem, veins and the ENLARGING CALYX. The maturing berry is HIDDEN inside a spiny burr-like calyx, unlike the exposed yellow berries of western horsenettle and silverleaf nightshade. Buffalobur is typically an annual, not a spreading perennial.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Solanaceae/Solanum: alternate leaves, 5-parted rotate or star-shaped corollas, poricidal anthers, and berry fruits; prickles and stellate hairs occur in many species.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: alternate green deeply 1–2 times pinnately lobed leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: FOUR shorter anthers plus ONE much longer curved darker-tipped anther

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx covered in long straw-colored prickles; calyx becomes larger as fruit matures

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: berry concealed within enlarged, spiny burr-like calyx

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Summer annual, erect to spreading and branching, often 0.2–0.6 m, frequently heavily armed with stiff yellowish prickles. Do not infer annuality from one photograph; use flowering/fruit structures to confirm.

key_traits.label: Leaf
key_traits.text: Simple ALTERNATE leaves, 1–2 times deeply pinnately lobed; lobes are often broad and rounded. Major leaf veins and petioles can also carry prickles. Inspect a mature leaf, not a newly unfolding one.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Five-lobed, fused BRIGHT YELLOW corolla, commonly about 1.5–3.5 cm across. Unlike the roughly equal yellow anthers of western horsenettle and silverleaf nightshade, buffalobur has four shorter yellow anthers and a conspicuously longer CURVED anther, often with a dusky reddish-purple tip. Anthers and style are DIFFERENT organs; don't label the slender style as the long anther.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: The calyx (joined sepals immediately behind the flower) becomes larger and densely prickly as fruit develops. It encloses the rounded fruit, creating a burr-like structure. Mature berry inside is typically small and brown/dry, not a large, freely exposed yellow berry.

key_traits.label: Prickles
key_traits.text: Check the calyx first, then the stems, petioles and main leaf veins for stiff straw-colored surface prickles. The prickly sphere in the photo is a CALYX enclosing the fruit, not the berry surface itself.

key_traits.label: Habitat
key_traits.text: Roadsides, disturbed soil, grazed ground and open dry sites. In the Hays/Edwards Plateau/Blackland Prairie encounter area, a familiar prickly summer annual; county-level native scoring remains deferred separately.

key_traits.label: Management
key_traits.text: Wear durable gloves and avoid gripping mature prickly burrs. If removing from a restoration bed, collect the bur-covered fruit before seed dispersal when practical, avoid disturbing desirable natives, and monitor seedlings. All parts should be treated as potentially toxic; never taste the fruit.

lookalikes.differences: Most useful pairings are western horsenettle and silverleaf nightshade. Flower/anther asymmetry and enclosing prickly fruit calyx diagnose buffalobur more reliably than the mere presence of prickles.
